title: Microburst-dampener KV-retention scheduler for low-jitter streaming chat
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a microburst-dampening batch formation heuristic that reduces latency jitter for streaming chat completions while maintaining high GPU utilization. The core idea is a lightweight admission + retention score for KV slots combined with a soft-window aggregation that adaptively extends batching windows during short microbursts and aggressively compacts KV into ephemeral slots under memory pressure. This ticket covers design decisions, simulator experiments, runtime changes for the allocator, and integration tests. Goals: preserve 99th percentile latency SLO, reduce token-cost overhead from unnecessary KV duplication, and improve steady-state GPU throughput in bursty workloads.

acceptance_criteria: Scheduler reduces 99th-percentile latency for replayed microburst traffic by >=15% vs baseline in the A/B test cluster.
No regression (>2%) in average latency on steady non-bursty workloads during canary rollout.
GPU memory overhead from KV replication across concurrent sessions does not increase by more than 5% in peak scenarios; if above, allocator must apply harder compaction heuristics.
Integration tests cover: EMA inter-arrival estimator, admission scoring, soft-window open/close, per-session cool-off, and eviction ordering under memory pressure.
PR reviewed and merged, with feature-flag gating and telemetry: metric names batcher.scheduler.microburst_enabled, batch.size.histogram, kv.slot_retention_count, kv.compactions.triggered.
implementation_notes: Estimator: use 64-bit fixed point EMA in hot path to avoid FP cost; alpha tunable per-customer.

Admission score components: priority (enterprise customers get additive score), expected added tokens (shorter sequences favored for quicker closes), session affinity (recently active sessions get bonus), retention_cost (estimated bytes if pinned).
Soft-window behavior: on microburst detection extend window by dynamic delta = base_delta * (1 + burst_factor), with capped max_window_ms=2000. Close window early if batch reaches target token count.
KV slot tagging: ephemeral_tag vs pinned_tag. Ephemeral slots are eligible for rapid compaction and can be relocated to shared compressed slots when eviction triggers.
GPU memory optimization: implement per-slab compaction hook after every N batch commits. Compaction will coalesce small KV fragments and evict ephemeral slots based on LRU+retention_score.
Fallback policies: when memory pressure > high_watermark or 95th token latency exceeds threshold, revert to strict hard-window=0 (latency-first) and increase preemption frequency.
Telemetry: add histograms for window_open_duration_ms, batch_token_count, retention_score_distribution, kv_eviction_reason.
Testing: use the replay harness with synthetic mixes: steady, microburst-short, microburst-long, adversarial (many long sessions), and e2e canary on 10% of production traffic behind feature flag.
